Poisson regression with HC3 robust standard errors

Source: R/hc3_stats.R
fit_poisson_hc3.Rd

Fits a log-link Poisson model with an offset by stats::glm.fit and reports selected coefficients with HC3 sandwich standard errors, which tolerate a variance different from the mean, and normal p-values.

Usage

fit_poisson_hc3(
  X,
  y,
  offset,
  terms = NULL,
  maxit = 100,
  min_rcond = 1e-12,
  max_abs_beta = 20
)

Arguments

X

Numeric design matrix (include the intercept column yourself).

y

Count response.

offset

Offset on the log scale, e.g. log(library_size / 1e4).

terms

Column names of X to report; NULL reports the last column.

maxit

Maximum number of IWLS iterations.

min_rcond, max_abs_beta

Thresholds of the "ill_conditioned" and "unstable" checks.

Value

A data.frame with one row per term: term, beta, se, p, n, status.

Details

Status codes: "rank_or_n" (n <= k + 20 or rank-deficient X), "nonconverged", "ill_conditioned" (reciprocal condition number of X' diag(mu) X below min_rcond), "unstable" (standard error zero or not finite, or |beta| > max_abs_beta), "ok".

Examples

set.seed(1)
X <- cbind(`(Intercept)` = 1, dose = rnorm(300))
depth <- runif(300, 5e3, 2e4)
y <- rpois(300, depth / 1e4 * exp(0.2 + 0.3 * X[, "dose"]))
fit_poisson_hc3(X, y, offset = log(depth / 1e4))
#>   term      beta        se            p   n status
#> 1 dose 0.3161844 0.0443064 9.586725e-13 300     ok
